Borylative Cyclization of 1,6-Allenynes Driven by BCl 3
Chun-Hua Yang, Xiangkun Sun, Congcong Niu, Zhiwei Zhang, Mingzhu Liu, Fangjie Zheng, Ling Jiang,
Xiangtao Kong, * and Zhantao Yang *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 8050 −8055 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A metal-free intramolecular borylative cyclization of 1,6-allenynes
driven by BCl 3 was developed. This method provides a general and practical strategy
to construct valuable pyrrolidines containing all-carbon quaternary centers or 3,5-
dihydroazepine derivatives depending on the substituents of the allene, with
conjugative and sterically hindered phenyl groups favoring the latter.
A
n attractive goal of organic synthesis is the selective
construction of highly functionalized polycyclic mole-
cules, which widely exist in natural products and have a broad
range of biological activities, in a step- and atom-economical
fashion.
1 Transition-metal-catalyzed cycloisomerization reac-
tions of 1, n-allenynes could be regarded as the most e ﬃcient
method in this regard, as they facilitate the rapid increase in
molecular complexity from simple linear substrates.
2 Since
Malacria’s pioneering work on the cobalt-catalyzed cyclo-
isomerization of 1,6-allenynes, 3 a variety of further-expanded
cycloisomerizations have been reported, which proceed
through trapping of the intermediates using nucleophilic,
oxidative, or reductive reagents.
4 In addition, by combining a
C−C bond-forming cyclization with borylation, complex
molecules suitable for diverse further functionalizations can
be acquired in one step.
5 However, examples that are involved
in cycloisomerization of 1, n-allenynes to generate borylated
molecules are still limited. The Ba ̈ckvall group has performed
seminal work in this area. In their systematic work, Ba ̈ckvall
and co-workers found that allenynes can undergo carbocycliza-
tion/borylation using a Pd(II) catalyst in the presence of
bis(pinacolato)diboron under di ﬀerent conditions to give
various boryl-functionalized ﬁve-membered rings ( Scheme
1a).
5c,6 The Ca ́rdenas group reported a formal hydroborylative
carbocyclization of allenynes to obtain allylboronates and
alkylboronates catalyzed by Pd(OAc)
2 (Scheme 1 b).5n
Although several borylativ e cycloisomerizations of 1, n-
allenynes have been disclosed, almost all of these methods
suﬀer from the demand for transition metals, and external
additives are usually needed. These requirements have limited
the substrate scope and practical applications. Therefore, it is
still essential and desirable to develop atom-economical and
metal-free methods for the direct preparation of various types
of boryl-functionalized polycyclic frameworks, especially those
bearing all-carbon quaternary centers, through cycloisomeriza-
tion of 1, n-allenynes.
Recently, the metal-free construction of C −B bonds has
attracted interest from the synthetic community.
7 In previous
work that is especially related to this study, Erker, Yamaguchi,
and co-workers discovered a novel borylative cyclization of 1,2-
dialkynylbenzenes using B(C
6F5)3 and in one example BCl 3 to
obtain dibenzopentalenes A and B. 8 Ingleson et al. presented
carbocyclization/borylation of a range of diynes to produce
boryl-functionalized cyclic compounds using BCl
3.9 However,
to the best of our knowledge, the current studies of metal-free
carbocyclization/borylation mainly focus on diynes. It is well-
known that allenes share many similar properties with alkynes.
It is still challenging but desirable to develop a metal-free
method for the construction of borylative all-carbon quaternary
stereocenters that would allow a series of derivatizations to
access structurally diverse molecules. As part of our work on
the formation of C −B bonds, we have for the ﬁrst time
discovered a metal-free carbocyclization/borylation of 1,6-
allenynes to a ﬀord diﬀerent borylvinyl pyrrolidines bearing all-
carbon quaternary stereocenters as well as 3,5-dihydroazepine
derivatives, which are among the challenging-ring-sized
skeletons in organic synthesis ( Scheme 1 c).
In our group, we are interested in extending BCl
3-induced
cyclization/borylation to unsaturated compounds, such as
alkenes and allenes.
10 We recently accomplished the direct
intramolecular aminoboration of sulfonamidoallenes using
BCl3 as the boron source, giving the desired products in

good yields. 10d Inspired by these results and Ingleson ’s work, 9
we decided to study the reaction between 1,6-allenynes and
BCl3 to further understand the BCl 3-involved cyclization/
borylation reactions on one hand and on the other to expand
the scope of the reaction.
To investigate the borylative cyclization of 1,6-allenynes,
initially our study was carried out with 1,6-allenyne 1a as the
model substrate and BCl
3 in a solution of CH 2Cl2 at ambient
temperature for 10 min ( Scheme 2 ). Gratifyingly, treatment
with pinacol and Et 3N gave the expected product 2a in 90%
isolated yield, and its structure was con ﬁrmed by NMR and
HRMS.
The functional group tolerance of the borylative cyclization
proved to be broad ( Scheme 3). First, substrates 1b−d bearing
a methyl substituent at the ortho, para,o r meta position of the
benzene ring and tert-butyl-substituted 1,6-allenyne 1e could
be subjected to the borylative cyclization smoothly and gave
the corresponding products in good yields. The structure of 2d
was also con ﬁrmed by single-crystal experiments. In contrast,
ether-containing substrate 1f gave an extremely low yield,
which may be ascribed to the cleavage of MeO (as a
nucleophile, the electron transfer of MeO-substituted phenyl-
acetylene promotes ether cleavage by attack of the anion on
Me
δ+) with BCl 3, resulting in a series of complex products.
When substrates with weak electron-withdrawing groups
such as F ( 1g) and Br ( 1h) on the benzene ring were subjected
to the reaction, the desired products were obtained in 84 −85%

yield. Moreover, 1,6-allenynes substituted with a relatively
stronger electron-withdrawing group such as an ester, CN, or
CF3 group were well-tolerated, providing the desired products
in 78 −89% yield. For example, substrate 1i with CF 3 at the
para position of the benzene ring gave borylative cyclization
product 2i in 89% yield. Substrates containing a Lewis basic
nitrile functionality often coordinate with strong boron
electrophiles, but in this case CN-containing alkyne 1j was
successfully cyclized and isolated in 78% yield under standard
conditions. Ester-containing substrate 1k was also amenable to
cyclization with 2 equiv of BCl 3, which might primarily result
from the coordination of the ester moiety with 1 equiv of BCl 3.
Moreover, 1,6-allenyne substrates substituted with naphthyl
and thienyl groups also underwent the cyclization to form 2l
and 2m, respectively. When the substrate with trisubstituted
allene ( 1n) was subjected to the reaction, the corresponding
product was obtained in 81% yield. When alkyl-substituted
alkyne 1o was subjected to the reaction, no product was
observed.
Next, reactions of phenyl-substituted 1,6-allenynes were
performed to further expand the scope of the reaction. When
substrate 3a was subjected to the reaction conditions, the
expected pyrrolidine analogue was not obtained. Treatment
with pinacol and Et
3N followed by isolation of the boronate
ester derivative enabled con ﬁrmation of the structure as the
3,5-dihydroazepine skeleton by single-crystal X-ray di ﬀraction
(Scheme 4 ). Encouraged by this result, we found that
substrates bearing electron-neutral ( 3a, 3b) or electron-
donating groups ( 3c) on the benzene ring were well-tolerated,
providing the desired products in 79 −87% yield, and electron-
withdrawing groups such as F ( 3d) and COOMe ( 3e) did not
decrease the yields. When alkyl-substituted alkyne 3f was
subjected to the reaction, the substrate disappeared and no
desired borylative cyclization product was detected.
With the aim of demonstrating the application potential of
the boronate compounds, functional group transformations
were studied with 2a as the model (see Scheme 5 ). With
sodium peroxoborate tetrahydrate as an oxidant, the Bpin
could be converted to OH, and ketone 5 was obtained as the
ﬁnal product. Suzuki coupling of 2a with iodobenzene gave the
corresponding product 6 in 82% yield. Treating 2a with
aqueous KHF
2 aﬀorded the desired tri ﬂuoroborate 7 (Scheme
5). Suzuki coupling of borylative cyclization product 4a with 1-
iodo-4-methylbenzene gave the corresponding product 8 in
83% yields.
According to our calculation results (for details, see the
Supporting Information), a relaxed scan of the potential energy
surface of BCl 3 approaching substrate 3a showed that BCl 3
attacks the carbon atom of the alkynyl group more easily.
Furthermore, for the phenyl-substituted substrates, electron
donor and conjugation e ﬀects can reduce the barrier of the
seven-membered ring pathway. Once formed, seven-mem-
bered-ring products will be produced smoothly, which might
result from formation of the stable carbocation. On the other
hand, because of steric hindrance by the phenyl group, the ﬁve-
membered-ring products are not easy to form. When the
substituent is methyl, the potential barrier allows only the
formation of ﬁve-membered-ring products, probably because
of the formation of the tertiary carbocation, which is consistent
with our experimental results. In addition, the magnitude of
the intermediate carbocation may be the key in controlling the
products.
The literature results showed that BCl
3 might serve as a
carbophilic Lewis acid, resulting in cyclization to zwitterions.
On the basis of literature results and the calculation results, a
tentative mechanism is proposed and is shown in Scheme 6 .
Taking 1a as an example, the complex consisting of substrate
1a and BCl
3 is formed upon the addition of BCl 3. Nucleophilic

attack on borylvinyl complex A along with C −B bond
formation can a ﬀord zwitterionic vinyl cation intermediate B,
which is rapidly converted to the corresponding alkenylboron
intermediate C. With 1,6-allenyne 3a, the phenyl groups would
strongly favor the formation of only seven-membered cyclized
intermediate F, which is consistent with the DFT calculations
(see the Supporting Information for details).
In summary, we have successfully developed the ﬁrst
eﬃcient metal-free intramolecular carbocyclization/borylation
of 1,6-allenynes with BCl 3,a ﬀording a rapid strategy for the
synthesis of a structurally diverse array of borylvinyl-
substituted N-heterocycles concomitant with the formation
of C−C and C −B bonds in good yields under mild conditions.
Importantly, the atom economy and operational simplicity
related to this method suggest its great potential for broad
applications in the construct ion of valuable borylvinyl
heterocycles in medical chemistry. DFT calculations suggested
that di ﬀerent cyclization sites are highly dependent on the
conjugative e ﬀect and the steric hindrance of substituents.
